Machines on-call for humans ©Resolve.ai - All rights reserved Announcing SRE-1, our first model, and Primary On-call SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - November 18, 2026 - ResolveAI today introduced SRE-1, a model trained to find the root cause of production alerts. On difficult live production incidents, SRE-1 dominates the Pareto frontier of pass rate against cost. Measured separately as a complete system, ResolveAI scores higher on production investigations than the coding-agent harnesses tested against it, with the widest margin on the hardest alerts. ResolveAI brings this research into its SRE agents that can now go on the critical path, starting with on-call, to drive reliability improvements. ResolveAI Primary On-call takes the page, closes what it can, and escalates to engineers only when needed, with an investigation attached. It also goes after the underlying issues that keep generating those pages. SRE-1 is available only through ResolveAI. Reliability now stops depending on how many engineers a company can keep on a rotation, and the hours they spent absorbing alerts go back into engineering. AI has transformed how software gets written and barely touched how it gets run. Models learned to write code from billions of published lines, whereas production offers no comparable public training corpus: no two companies run the same system, incidents stay private, root causes are never written down, and the evidence an investigation depends on expires within weeks. General-purpose models, however capable, arrive at an incident without knowledge of the environment they are asked to investigate, and a larger model does not change that, because the answer was never written down anywhere to be learned. It exists only in the running system, reachable by making the right queries against that system, in the right order, and judging what comes back before the evidence ages out. That is work a domain-specific model for production has to be trained for, not knowledge it can be handed from the internet. "No engineering team can keep up with how fast code and patches land in production. The answer is agents that are accurate and fast enough to sit on the critical path, and that takes a model built for production. On hard production incidents, SRE-1 is the most accurate model at every budget we measured, including frontier models. At that level of accuracy and cost, investigating every alert and fixing what sits behind it becomes practical," said Spiros Xanthos, co-founder and CEO of ResolveAI. SRE-1 is a 27B model built on open weights, trained by a team of 16 AI researchers over a final run of 7.4 days on up to 512 GPUs. On 49 difficult live production cases, each run five times, an ensemble of five SRE-1 investigations matches the strongest frontier model the company tested, at lower cost. Training used reinforcement learning alone, which took a single investigation's pass rate from 6.9% to 38.8% on the same incidents with the same tools. Every tool in training was pinned to the moment the alert fired, so the model could not read the answer from the future. Primary On-call holds the pager: it takes the page, closes what it can, and escalates only when an engineer is needed. On each page, it investigates across telemetry, infrastructure, code, and operational knowledge. It then closes the alert, mitigates the problem where a team's policies permit, or escalates when human judgment is needed. After it acts, it checks the fix against the production baseline and keeps watching until recovery holds. In production, Primary On-call handles up to 80% of paged alerts without escalating to a human, and customers report a 10x improvement in mean time to resolution, with up to 95% root-cause accuracy on investigations. Existing paging-system timeouts remain as an independent backstop, and Resolve records every investigation and decision so engineers can review what it found and why it acted. "ResolveAI has been part of how our CRM Analytics team handles incidents, so extending it to ResolveAI Primary On-call was the natural next step. In the first few weeks of our dark launch testing, ResolveAI has closed more than 70% of our paging alerts without waking an engineer, with high accuracy. That's why we're ready to put ResolveAI Primary On-call in our paging path as our first responder," said Bhupesh Patel, Software Engineering Principal Architect at Salesforce. An alert that is answered but never fixed keeps firing, and so does every other alert the same underlying problem produces. Fixing that problem stops the alerts and removes a source of future incidents. Primary On-call connects related alerts and investigations into a shared view of each underlying problem. Across a team's services, those views add up to a running picture of service health that the team can keep improving. It carries the production evidence and investigation history into the fix, applies it within the scope a team has approved, then monitors it to confirm it holds. The evidence and the full audit trail stay with the issue. Teams build trust before handing anything over. On the alerts a team knows best, Resolve works every page and records the call it would have made while the existing rotation continues unchanged, so engineers can grade its judgment against pages they already know the answer to. Primary On-call takes the rotation only on the alert rules where that record has earned it. Primary On-call is generally available today. SRE-1 is available only through ResolveAI. For more information, visit resolve.ai. ResolveAI is the AI Lab building models and SRE agents that automate production. Founded by Spiros Xanthos and Mayank Agarwal, co-creators of OpenTelemetry, it trains its own models, including SRE-1, and puts its agents on the critical path: taking the pager, mitigating incidents, fixing underlying issues, and automating the day-to-day work of production.
